the development of a new therapeutic approach for the treatment of colorectal cancer.

Folfox-induced adaptive resistance is associated to the expression and the secretion of PD-L1 in the tumor micro-environment, which could be targeted by anti-PD1 treatment.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of immune-checkpoint blockade therapy in combination to chemotherapies could improve clinical outcomes in cancer patients.
the PD-1 pathway is involved in the adaptive immune resistance mechanism induced by chemotherapy in colorectal tumors.
chemotherapy induces an adaptive immune resistance in the form of PD-1/PDL1 pathway activation in the tumor micro environment and this can be overcome by checkpoint blockade therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Folfox is able to induce tumor infiltration of PD-1+CD8 T cells and PD-L1 expression on tumor cells, leading to adaptive immune resistance in the tumor microenviroment.
Folfox induces tumor adaptive immune resistance through the PD-1 pathway, leading to tumor cure when combined to PD-1 blockade.
Folfox induces adaptive immune resistance in a PD-1/PDL-1 dependent manner.
